entries.title: The first pool
entries.text: A tide-pup left its wet mark on a rock crab. A spark-bred friend stepped close, and the water answered with a crack of light.

entries.title: Low water
entries.text: When the tide drops, water-folk grow bold and quick. A quick one steps aside before the wave can reach it. The slow ones always get wet.

entries.title: Warm stone
entries.text: A hot rock dropped into a cold pool throws up so much fog that nobody can see their own paws. The loudest one wins.

entries.title: A small friend
entries.text: The mist-newts stand at the back and hum. Everyone in front of them stands a little taller, and nobody can say why.

entries.title: A lucky hit
entries.text: Now and then a splash lands exactly right and the rock splits clean. It happens about once in twenty, and it never feels planned.

entries.title: Green at the mouth
entries.text: Vines had crept over the cave mouth. One spark, and the whole hillside roared. Nothing green was left by morning.

entries.title: Where the sea comes in
entries.text: A wave rolled into the hot cave and came back as a white wall of hot fog. Everything that was glowing went dark for a breath.

entries.title: The ash burrow
entries.text: The diggers keep their burrows warm and call everyone in. A team that shares a burrow glows with it for a few rounds, and hits a little harder while it lasts.

entries.title: Sunlight in the deep
entries.text: Far down, where no sun reaches, a mane of light walks first and everyone else walks in its glow. It leaves a scorch on whatever it passes.

entries.title: Cooling off
entries.text: Even the hottest rock cools if you wait for the right moment. The ones who rush in early get burned, and the ones who wait get paid.

entries.title: Heavy bark
entries.text: The bark-wardens stand in the front and take the blows. They carry more weight than they look, and they never say so.

entries.title: Roots and a bolt
entries.text: Something crackling with charge once crossed the hollow. Roots burst from the ground, caught it, and pulled it down in a single flash.

entries.title: A garden on a shell
entries.text: A turtle with a garden on its back plants a seed in whatever it meets. Others come along later and harvest it.

entries.title: Brambles at both ends
entries.text: The old queen of thorns binds the creatures at the ends of every row. The ones in the middle of a row are always the ones who get out.

entries.title: A wall of moss
entries.text: One quiet word and the moss rose up in a wall. For a moment, half the hollow could stand in front of anything.

entries.title: The lightning rod
entries.text: The king of the clouds always picks out the strongest creature on the ridge and strikes it first. The weakest walk home unharmed.

entries.title: First in, first out
entries.text: The mice zip in ahead of everyone and leave the sky humming behind them. Whatever follows them gets all the credit.

entries.title: A wet wire
entries.text: A drenched beast that meets a spark makes the whole ridge hum, and the sound goes on for a full minute. Nobody wants to be next to it.

entries.title: The edge of the cloud
entries.text: The rays ride the very edge of a storm. They hit hard and fast, and most of the time they hit exactly where they aimed.

entries.title: The watcher above
entries.text: Far above the thunder, a ribbon of light hangs over the team and keeps everyone's spirits high. The crowd has never seen its face.

entries.title: Which end first
entries.text: Some beasts take their turn strictly from the left. Others begin at the right end of the road. Learn which one you are facing.

entries.title: Fast feet
entries.text: Some beasts are quick on their feet. A quick creature can step aside and let a hit go by. The quickest do it often, and the slow hardly ever.

entries.title: Front, middle, back
entries.text: A hard blow aimed at the front rarely reaches the back. The ones in the rear can stay calm and let the front do the shouting.

entries.title: Who pays the toll
entries.text: At every crossing one friend marks the road and another takes the prize. The best teams put the marker first.

entries.title: The wishing well
entries.text: Travellers say the well gives back a little of what you drop in. Three coins buy a better road, and the rest are only for luck.

entries.title: A fork in the fur
entries.text: Two of the same kind rarely walk the same road twice. The second one always comes back a little stronger than the first.

entries.title: The silver tide
entries.text: Only at night does the water pull back far enough to show the coral. By morning it is gone, and nobody remembers the way.

entries.title: A lance of coral
entries.text: The coral cats strike from shadow and rarely miss. They are proud of it, and a little proud of their crowns.

entries.title: A glowing wall
entries.text: At the deepest edge the reef lights up like a wall. Anything that hides behind it takes half the weight of a blow.

entries.title: The night singer
entries.text: Something sings across the water that makes the boss forget its counter-move for a few breaths. Then it stops, and all is quiet.

entries.title: Fog on the reef
entries.text: The newts tuck their friends into the fog and the boss cannot see where to aim. Nobody has ever caught one asleep.

entries.title: Paper lanterns
entries.text: The lantern fish lights the way and lends a hand. Its glow makes a drenched foe easy to mark again, even in the dark.

entries.title: The hearth ward
entries.text: A tortoise with a bonfire on its shell shields a whole row at once for three rounds. The fire never goes out.

entries.title: Bunting and ribbons
entries.text: The festival boss is always a little easier than the last one. Everybody is in too good a mood to be afraid of it.

entries.title: The last night
entries.text: On the last night the whole meadow goes quiet for a moment, then fireworks open the sky and everyone remembers why they came.

entries.title: Bait and patience
entries.text: Every explorer learns the same thing in the end: the creatures come to the ones who wait, and the quiet ones wait best.

entries.title: The rare hour
entries.text: Rarer things show themselves to those who go further and stay longer. A short walk finds the common ones, a long one finds the rest.

entries.title: An old friend
entries.text: A creature that comes back often learns the way. After a few trips it finds the hidden corners without a lantern at all.

entries.title: It remembers
entries.text: Bosses learn. After the first night of a hard fight, the big ones come back with a new trick and a long memory.

entries.title: The wheel of elements
entries.text: Water puts out fire, fire eats the green, the green drinks lightning, and lightning splits the water. The wheel has never once stopped.

entries.title: The chart of elements
entries.text: Water puts out fire, fire eats the green, the green drinks lightning, and lightning splits the water. But the wheel was never the whole world: in the fen, the mud drinks the flame.
